analysis: H-C01-5 holds for all 756 relations with an unbordered side; 81 of the 281 relations with both sides bordered deviate from the generic count, all sharing a common border.
assumptions: alphabets of size 2 (k = 2..5, n <= 12) and 3 (k = 2..3, n <= 7)
falsification: Any relation with an unbordered side whose class counts differ from the series.

history.new: H-C01-5 holds for all 756 relations with an unbordered side; 81 of the 281 relations with both sides bordered deviate from the generic count, all sharing a common border.

hypothesis: H-C01-5: if |u| = |v| = k, u != v and u is unbordered (no proper prefix equals a suffix), then the number of classes of length-n words over a q-letter alphabet equals [x^n] 1/(1 - q x + x^k), i.e. the number of length-n words avoiding u.
methodology: Exhaustive over all unordered pairs {u, v} of distinct words of length k. Exact class counts by union-find; compare with the series coefficients; for relations whose sides are both bordered, record counts, the minimal linear recurrence fitted to them, and whether shortlex completion terminates.
question: Why do all length-3 relations give F(n+3)-1 classes and most length-4 relations give partial sums of tribonacci numbers? Which relations are exceptions?
